title: Disjoint union of two proper schemes over a base is proper
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $p_1:W_1\to S$ and $p_2:W_2\to S$ morphisms of schemes, $W=W_1\amalg W_2$ the disjoint union (coproduct in the category of schemes) with coprojections $\iota_1:W_1\to W$, $\iota_2:W_2\to W$, and $p:W\to S$ the morphism with $p\circ\iota_k=p_k$ ($k=1,2$). (1) $\iota_1$ and $\iota_2$ are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion] and the underlying set of $W$ is the disjoint union of $\iota_1(W_1)$ and $\iota_2(W_2)$. (2) If $p_1$ and $p_2$ are proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], then $p$ is proper.

proof.text: *Step 1 (part (1)).* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family] to the family $(W_1,W_2)$ indexed by $I=\{1,2\}$: the coproduct $W=W_1\amalg W_2$ exists, the coprojections $\iota_1,\iota_2$ are open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], $\iota_1(W_1)\cap\iota_2(W_2)=\emptyset$ and $\iota_1(W_1)\cup\iota_2(W_2)=W$. This is (1). Write $U_k=\iota_k(W_k)$; $U_1,U_2$ are open, and each is closed as the complement of the other. Since $\iota_k$ is an open immersion, it is a homeomorphism of $W_k$ onto $U_k$ and an isomorphism of schemes $W_k\to U_k$ onto the open subscheme $U_k$; as $p\circ\iota_k=p_k$, this isomorphism is one over $S$ (with $p|_{U_k}$ on $U_k$). For (2) assume $p_1,p_2$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], i.e. separated, of finite type and universally closed; Steps 2 to 4 show that $p$ has these three properties, which by definition [def-weil-proper-morphism] is (2).

proof.text: *Step 2 ($p$ is of finite type).* Let $V=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq S$ be an affine open. Since $W=U_1\cup U_2$ and $p\circ\iota_k=p_k$, we have $p^{-1}(V)=\iota_1(p_1^{-1}(V))\cup\iota_2(p_2^{-1}(V))$. As $p_k$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], $p_k^{-1}(V)$ is covered by finitely many affine opens $V_{k,j}=\operatorname{Spec}B_{k,j}$ ($j=1,\dots,n_k$) with $B_{k,j}$ a finitely generated $A$-algebra via $p_k$. By Step 1, $\iota_k$ maps $V_{k,j}$ isomorphically onto the open subscheme $\iota_k(V_{k,j})$ of $W$ [def-weil-open-immersion], so $\iota_k(V_{k,j})$ is an affine open of $W$ with ring $B_{k,j}$, and since $p\circ\iota_k=p_k$ its $A$-algebra structure via $p$ is the one via $p_k$. The finitely many affine opens $\iota_k(V_{k,j})$ ($k=1,2$, $j\le n_k$) cover $p^{-1}(V)$ and are spectra of finitely generated $A$-algebras; hence $p$ is locally of finite type, $p^{-1}(V)$ is quasi-compact (a finite union of quasi-compact sets), and $p$ is of finite type by [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] (its 'equivalently, finite affine cover' clause).

proof.text: *Step 3 ($p$ is universally closed).* Let $g:T\to S$ be a morphism of schemes, $W_T=W\times_ST$ [def-pc-fibre-product] with projections $q:W_T\to W$ and $p_T:W_T\to T$, and $W_{k,T}=W_k\times_ST$ with projection $p_{k,T}:W_{k,T}\to T$. By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with $X=W$, $Y=T$, $V=U_k$, $W=T$, $U=S$) the canonical morphism $U_k\times_ST\to W_T$ is an open immersion with image $q^{-1}(U_k)$, compatibly with the projections to $T$; composing with the isomorphism $W_{k,T}\to U_k\times_ST$ induced by the isomorphism $W_k\cong U_k$ over $S$ of Step 1 gives an open immersion $j_k:W_{k,T}\to W_T$ with image $q^{-1}(U_k)$ and $p_T\circ j_k=p_{k,T}$. Since $U_1,U_2$ partition $W$, the opens $q^{-1}(U_1),q^{-1}(U_2)$ partition $W_T$. Let $Z\subseteq W_T$ be closed. Then $Z=(Z\cap q^{-1}(U_1))\cup(Z\cap q^{-1}(U_2))$ and $p_T(Z\cap q^{-1}(U_k))=p_T(j_k(j_k^{-1}(Z)))=p_{k,T}(j_k^{-1}(Z))$. The set $j_k^{-1}(Z)$ is closed in $W_{k,T}$ ($j_k$ continuous), and $p_{k,T}$ is a closed map because $p_k$ is universally closed [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Hence $p_T(Z)=p_{1,T}(j_1^{-1}Z)\cup p_{2,T}(j_2^{-1}Z)$ is closed in $T$, so $p_T$ is closed for every $T\to S$, i.e. $p$ is universally closed.

source.place: Schemes, Definition 01KB (universally closed) and Morphisms, Definition 01W1 (proper); Schemes, Lemma 01JR (open subschemes of fibre products); written out by the worker

proof.text: *Step 4 ($p$ is separated).* Let $\mathrm{pr}_1,\mathrm{pr}_2:W\times_SW\to W$ be the projections [def-pc-fibre-product] and $A_{kl}=\mathrm{pr}_1^{-1}(U_k)\cap\mathrm{pr}_2^{-1}(U_l)$ ($k,l\in\{1,2\}$). As $U_1,U_2$ partition $W$, the four opens $A_{kl}$ partition $W\times_SW$, so each is also closed (its complement is the union of the other three). By [lem-weil-pbc-open-fibre-product] (with $X=Y=W$, $V=W=U_k$, $U=S$), $U_k\times_SU_k\to W\times_SW$ is an open immersion with image $A_{kk}$; composed with the isomorphism $W_k\times_SW_k\cong U_k\times_SU_k$ from Step 1 this gives an open immersion $m_k=\iota_k\times_S\iota_k:W_k\times_SW_k\to W\times_SW$ with image $A_{kk}$, a homeomorphism onto $A_{kk}$. Both $\Delta_p\circ\iota_k$ and $m_k\circ\Delta_{p_k}$ have both projections equal to $\iota_k$, so $\Delta_p\circ\iota_k=m_k\circ\Delta_{p_k}$ by the universal property of the fibre product, and $\Delta_p(W)=m_1(\Delta_{p_1}(W_1))\cup m_2(\Delta_{p_2}(W_2))$. Since $p_k$ is separated, $\Delta_{p_k}$ is a closed immersion [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], so $\Delta_{p_k}(W_k)$ is closed in $W_k\times_SW_k$; its image under the homeomorphism $m_k$ onto $A_{kk}$ is closed in $A_{kk}$, hence closed in $W\times_SW$ because $A_{kk}$ is closed. So $\Delta_p(W)$ is closed, a union of two closed sets. The diagonal $\Delta_p$ is an immersion [lem-weil-pbc-diagonal-immersion] with closed image, hence a closed immersion [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-closed-image-closed-immersion], i.e. $p$ is separated [def-weil-proper-morphism].
